newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sleepy DAX hobbled by dollar uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Sleepy DAX hobbled by dollar uncertainties.

text.p: German shares crawled sideways at lower levels in afternoon trade on Monday in what dealers said was a tentative start to a week likely to be plagued by currency-related uncertainties.

The dollar's slide against the mark was the trigger for the slight fall in German share prices and dealers said tensions would persist before the International Monetary Fund meeting in Washington this weekend, which could yield key dollar comments.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was down 24.66 points at 3,336.54 points at 1406 GMT, some ten points below the DAX's mid-afternoon bourse close.
"If we see another five or ten pfennigs off the dollar, that's going to be really bad news," said a Frankfurt trader.
"All this currency talk could bring us pretty much to our knees this week."
Industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG came under the most dollar-driven pressure and was down 2.35 marks at 128.05 marks in afternoon trade.

Dealers said Daimler's problems were exacerbated by a report in the Bild newspaper that Bonn was planning to sharply raise petrol tax. The government denied its plans, but that had little bearing on the markets.
However Siemens AG was up 83 pfennigs at 89.96 marks ahead of its first half earnings report this week and SAP to 293 marks as investors looked to its first quarter report due on Tuesday.
Sports retail group Puma AG and Adidas were under pressure after news earlier this month that U.S. rival Nike plans to cut production capacity.
Puma was down 3.25 marks, or 5.4 percent at 56.75 marks while Adidas fell five marks, or 2.8 percent to 153 marks.
Gains and losses were otherwise generally modest and mixed.

Dealers also noted that uncertainty about the direction of U.S. interest rates was still a source of anxiety and said recent talk of a possible delay of Europe's currency union or a weakening of the euro launch criteria was also making investors unwilling to make a move.
"The renewed euro talk could certainly push the DAX back toward 3,200 points," said Trinkaus Capital Management in a note to investors.
Before than, most dealers saw strong psychological support for the DAX at 3,300 points.
